caption: NOT gate with a lever input (track gates): the lever strongly powers the stone it hangs on; a torch on top of that stone inverts it. 2 gt.
OR gate with lever inputs (track gates): both levers hang on one stone and strongly power it; the output cell above the stone sees it. 0 gt, one block.
NOR gate with lever inputs (track gates): both levers hang on the same stone and strongly power it; a torch on top of the stone is lit only when neither lever is on. 2 gt.

OR gate, instant (track gates): one dust on a stone between the two inputs; either input powers the dust, the dust powers the stone under it, and the output cell under the stone sees it. 0 gt. (With the output cell itself between the inputs the OR needs no block at all.)
NOT gate, 2 gt (track gates): the input powers a dust on a stone; the dust powers the stone under it, and a wall torch on the stone's side goes out. The output cell is under the torch.
NIMPLY under R7: input b arrives on the design's own repeater, which outputs into a dust that feeds the subtract comparator's side (a comparator side reads only dust, a redstone block or a diode).
NIMPLY under R7: input b arrives on the design's own repeater, which outputs into a dust that feeds the subtract comparator's side (a comparator side reads only dust, a redstone block or a diode).
NOR with real signal inputs: one dust between the two inputs (either input powers it, that is OR), on a stone whose wall torch is lit only when the dust is off. 2 gt, 3 blocks.

IMPLY (NOT a OR b): a's input block carries a torch, lit when a is off; that torch and input b both power the output dust between them. The b input never sits on the torch, so the gate is steady at rest. 2 gt, 5 blocks.

IMPLY (NOT a OR b): a's input block carries a torch, lit when a is off; that torch and input b both power the output dust between them. The b input never sits on the torch, so the gate is steady at rest. 2 gt, 5 blocks.

XOR with real signal inputs: two subtract comparators, C reading a at its back and b at its side, D reading b at its back and a at its side, both pointing into the same output cell. Each input also travels the long way round to a repeater that feeds the other comparator's side, and the repeater is what makes the gate exact: it restores the signal to 15, so a comparator sees back and side equal when both inputs are on and subtracts to zero. Without it the detoured signal arrives weaker and the gate behaves as OR. 4 gt.

XNOR with real signal inputs: the XOR core (two subtract comparators, each reading one input at its back and the other at its side, restored to full strength by a repeater on the detour) pointing into a stone instead of an air cell, with a torch on top of that stone: the stone is powered exactly when the inputs differ, so the torch is lit exactly when they agree. 6 gt.

NAND with real signal inputs: a torch stands on each input block, so each goes out when its input turns on; the dust between them, on its own support stone, is therefore lit unless BOTH inputs are on. 2 gt, 4 blocks.

AND with real signal inputs: a torch stands on each input block, so each goes out when its input turns on; the dust between them is then off exactly when both inputs are on, and the wall torch hanging under that dust turns it back into AND. 4 gt, 5 blocks.
